opportunities.title: Junior Scientist Conference Grant

amount.raw: Scheme A up to £200; Scheme B up to £500 (up to £750 for Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored awards); Scheme C up to £300

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to Genetics Society junior scientist members. Scheme A: undergraduate, Master's and PhD student members and postdoctoral members within 6 years of PhD viva. Schemes B & C: PhD student and postdoctoral members within 6 years of PhD viva. Applicants must present a poster or give a talk at the conference. Supervisors providing support letters must be current members.
opportunities.summary: Supports attendance of Genetics Society junior scientist members at conferences on genetics research. Three streams: (A) attendance at Genetics Society/SIG meetings (up to £200); (B) attendance at non-Genetics Society meetings (up to £500, or up to £750 for Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored awards); (C) registration for virtual conferences (up to £300).

opportunities.title: Training Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society can apply, as long as studying or working in the UK, or the course is held in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others should be members for at least one year. Supervisors must be members.
opportunities.summary: Grants of up to £1,200 to enable members to attend formal short training courses, or a collaborative visit to another laboratory to train in specific genetic/genomic techniques. Covers travel, accommodation, subsistence and registration/tuition fees.

opportunities.title: Heredity Fieldwork Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society can apply, as long as studying or working in the UK, or intending to carry out fieldwork in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others should be members for at least one year. Supervisors must be members.
opportunities.summary: Awards up to £2,000 to cover travel and accommodation costs associated with a field-based genetic research project, funded by income from the Society's journal Heredity. Research should produce results suitable for publication in Heredity.

opportunities.title: Carer's Award
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Any Genetics Society member can apply, regardless of age of the person they are caring for. Priority given to early-career scientists and according to need.
opportunities.summary: Award of up to £60/day to support members with caring responsibilities to attend Society meetings and events, to be used as the awardee thinks best supports their attendance.

opportunities.title: One-off Meeting Grant

amount.raw: Several levels of sponsorship: a specific lecture for a few hundred pounds, a session up to about £1,000, major sponsorship of an entire meeting potentially several thousand pounds (recent major sponsorships £1,000-£2,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to Genetics Society members. Meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of genetic-themed meetings not organised directly by the Genetics Society. Grants are used towards the organisation of a meeting (not attendance), with several levels of sponsorship available.

opportunities.title: Public Engagement Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to members of the Genetics Society.
opportunities.summary: Grants of up to £1,000 to support public engagement activities related to genetics, delivered in person or virtually. Funding may cover eligible travel and materials costs.

opportunities.title: Special Interest Group (SIG) Funding
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to Genetics Society members. Meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK.
opportunities.summary: Funding up to £2,000 per year for genetics research communities who wish to run regular series of meetings (Special Interest Groups). Applications to become a new SIG should be submitted at least three months before the first meeting.
